clue.text: Don't start to gamble — take your client's money

indicators.note: refusing to start means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to gamble on a risky venture is to speculate

explanation.surface: A warning to a financial adviser: don't start gambling, or you'll end up stealing your client's money.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to embezzle funds entrusted to your care, such as money held for someone else.

clue.text: Caper in which Pope's head — was head — of the national church

indicators.note: this phrase sets up one letter standing where another one was
one letter takes over the spot previously held by the leading letter

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of Pope
the Gallican national church is the church of France, read here as the nation

explanation.surface: A quip about a pope taking over as head of a country's church.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of the nation's name, F, gives way to the Pope's head, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap about playfully, and to prance is to spring or bound in a lively way.

clue.text: Fair bit of hair — depending on neck size?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hair grown long enough to reach the shirt neck
second meaning, playful: a measurement governed by the size of a shirt's neckband

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as whimsical: the length of a collar does depend on the wearer's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair worn down to the shirt collar is a fair amount, and a shirt collar's measurement is set by the neck it encircles.

clue.text: First of Walter Mitty's turns: provide defence and make me conform

indicators.note: turning things over and round changes their order, so the letters get rearranged
the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Walter
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to arm is to equip with weapons for defence

explanation.surface: Walter Mitty, Thurber's daydreamer, takes his turn to arm himself and is pressed into line.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's fantasist; his name merely supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: "Twist my arm" is the idiom for being persuaded or pressured into going along with something, usually jokingly.

clue.text: Cut the grass round the pub for the little drinker?

definitions.note: the whole phrase stands for a small fish

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Mowing the lawn around the pub as a treat for a small drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: People drink like a fish, so a little fish is a little drinker; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a tiny freshwater fish, and fish are proverbial heavy drinkers.

clue.text: It includes something of a concession, no less? You don't surprise me

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: taken as written
a conjunction used to concede a point, as in 'though it rained'
'as much' means no less than that amount

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a remark was a concession, then shrugs off an unsurprising reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying "I thought as much" means you had already suspected it, so the news is no surprise to you.

clue.text: How I ensure mine's top?

parts.note: surface reading: a boast about making sure my product or entry wins
setter's reading: 'mine' means my own people, my relatives, placed in the top jobs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' seems to mean my thing, but it means my family, whom I promote.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives with posts and appointments, regardless of merit, is the practice of favouritism toward family.

clue.text: Don't go straight at rapid pace through the Cotswolds

definitions.note: describes a river by where it flows

parts.note: to wind is to twist and turn rather than go straight
a rush is a hurried pace

explanation.surface: A meandering stream hurrying through the Cotswold hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are hills in south-west England; the Windrush is a river flowing through them to the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windrush is the river that winds through the Cotswold hills before joining the Thames.

clue.text: Continent, not island, shortly to be put in geography book

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another piece

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: said shortly, the word is clipped as in a contraction

parts.note: taken as written
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a land mass counts as continent or island in a geography textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' clipped becomes NT, as in contractions like don't.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary lost continent said by Plato to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Composer's church work fashionable?

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
op. is short for opus, a musical work
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Asking whether a composer's sacred piece is in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was the Polish Romantic pianist famous for his nocturnes and mazurkas.

clue.text: Art possessor in town with belt?

definitions.note: cryptic: the virtue that comes with a belt

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: a city is a large town
the one who 'art' also 'hast': archaic second-person forms of be and have

explanation.surface: An art collector in a town, wearing a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: Thou art and thou hast are old forms of you are and you have, so the owner in that archaic voice hast.
explanation.definitionFit: A chastity belt is the medieval device supposedly locked on to enforce sexual abstinence, hence the virtue goes with a belt.

clue.text: Gambler gives money to the Irish queen

parts.note: the punt was the Irish pound before the euro
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A gambler hands cash to an Irish queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter is someone who places bets, especially on horse races.

clue.text: Races for spinner in which one's performing

indicators.note: something in which others sit holds them inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a mule is a spinning machine used in cotton mills
a means one
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: Racing on behalf of a bowler who is playing in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinning mule is the cotton machine invented by Samuel Crompton, not a cricket bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula One is the top class of motor racing, a series of Grand Prix races.

clue.text: Suggestion to relative following river through Kentish town

indicators.note: coming after places one piece at the end of another
running through something puts it inside

parts.note: Hythe is a town on the Kent coast
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: Directions to a relative about a river crossing a Kent town.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation put forward for testing, a tentative proposal.

clue.text: A student at studios in Hertfordshire

definitions.note: stands for a place found in that county

parts.note: taken as written
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
Denham Film Studios were in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A film student working at studios in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertfordshire is an English county just north of London; Aldenham is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldenham is a village and parish near Watford in the English home county of Hertfordshire.

clue.text: With the services a fellow might have had a commission

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a commission confers authority to act

explanation.surface: A man in the armed forces who might have been made an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manpower means the people available for work or military duty, the strength of personnel in the forces.

clue.text: Belladonna produced work of art? Say what you think

indicators.note: something worked is reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to opine is to state your opinion

explanation.surface: An art critic asks whether a painting of belladonna is truly art.
explanation.walkthrough: Belladonna is deadly nightshade, a poisonous plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is the poisonous alkaloid extracted from deadly nightshade, used medically to dilate the pupils.

clue.text: See 23
Love among the olive trees? Is this a record?

definitions.note: cryptic: the part of a record holding the sound

indicators.note: being among things means sitting within them

parts.note: olive trees grow in groves
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A romance in an olive grove, and a question whether it sets a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is the spiral track cut into a vinyl disc, carrying the sound.

clue.text: Beast painted by Kipling and loved by Precott

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the big cat Kipling drew for his Just So Stories
second meaning: the luxury car, of which John Prescott famously had two

explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott, Labour Deputy Prime Minister, was nicknamed Two Jags for his official and private cars; the clue misspells his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a big spotted American cat, and the same name belongs to a British make of luxury car.

clue.text: See 6
Setter's reversing manoeuvre to provide a job

indicators.note: going into reverse runs the word backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a ploy is a tactical manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A setter's three-point turn as a way of creating work.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone is to give them paid work, to hire them.

clue.text: Autostradas' radiation is implied in every way by metal (gold) in the book

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

parts.note: every way, read as every route
lead is a metal
a tome is a large book
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A musing on how Italy's motorways fan out, with a metallic book thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Autostradas are Italian motorways, imagined radiating from the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says every route ends at the same place, as Roman roads all led from the empire's capital.

clue.text: The last state may fruit with the first two…

parts.note: may is the hawthorn, whose fruit is the haw
A is the first letter
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fruit of a final condition, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: May is a British name for hawthorn blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii was the fiftieth and most recently admitted of the United States, joining in 1959.

clue.text: …unpaid: nothing for the singer at its head

definitions.note: its capital, following on from the previous clue

parts.note: Hon. is short for honorary, an unpaid post
O is zero
Lulu is the Scottish pop singer

explanation.surface: An unpaid singer gets nothing at the top of the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the previous clue, 'its' means Hawaii's.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of Hawaii, the head of the state's government.

clue.text: King to be (French brand) in progress — hence all those surveys

parts.note: King Mark of Cornwall, from the Tristan legend
être is French for to be
a brand sears, and searing kept going is read as a search

explanation.surface: A would-be king with a French label at work, prompting survey after survey.
explanation.definitionFit: Market research is the gathering of consumer opinion through questionnaires and polls.
